newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent stagnates at lower levels, awaits NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent stagnates at lower levels, awaits NYMEX.

text.p: IPE Brent futures stagnated at slightly lower levels on Wednesday with most of the market sidelined ahead of NYMEX's open, traders said.
June IPE Brent was trading four cents lower at $18.57 a barrel, while gas oil was $1.50 up at $170.25 a tonne.
"We're basically waiting for the U.S. to open," said one trader. He said there was stubborn resistance at $18.64.
"It's a very sensitive level. The market shed 70 cents when it touched $18.64 last week," one trader said referring to price action on April 22.
Traders had been hoping the June contract would make an assault on $18.77 which marks the top of a downside gap which has capped the market over the last three weeks.
"It hasn't tried to close it on its own," said another player. "Players are waiting to see what NYMEX does."
Gas oil, meanwhile, pushed higher as it played catch-up with IPE Brent and NYMEX futures gains posted after the gas oil market closed.

Traders said gas oil was also being supported by mildly bullish American Petroleum Institute data which showed U.S. middle distillate stocks grew by 1.4 million barrels last week. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
